name: EU Blue Card (Niebieska Karta UE)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an employment contract, homework (nakładcza) contract, or civil-law contract of at least 6 months' duration, paid in PLN through the Polish payroll system.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying contract from a Polish employer of at least 6 months.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires higher education qualifications relevant to the role, or at least 5 years of comparable professional experience as an alternative route to qualifying.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain recognition of a foreign degree, or document 5+ years of relevant professional experience.

requirements.blocker_text: Gross monthly salary must be at least 150% of the national average wage in the preceding calendar year -- PLN 13,355.34/month as of the February 2026 GUS announcement for 2025's average wage.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a higher salary or wait for a new employer offer at or above the current threshold.

evidence_required.document: Employment or civil-law contract of at least 1 year, meeting the salary threshold
Degree recognition or documented professional experience

outcome.duration_length: contract duration + 3 months, up to a maximum of 3 years
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 5 years total in the EU, of which at least 2 years immediately before the application must be in Poland, count toward the EU long-term resident permit specifically (a faster combined-mobility path than the plain 5-year Polish-only residence requirement)

notes: LIVE THRESHOLD CATCH, same pattern as Germany's Blue Card and the UK/Netherlands/France salary re-basings: the Blue Card threshold is not a fixed number, it's 150% of GUS's announced average national wage for the prior year, re-published every February. The 2025 threshold was PLN 12,272.58/month (150% of 2024's PLN 8,181.72 average); the 2026 threshold, announced 9 Feb 2026, is PLN 13,355.34/month (150% of 2025's PLN 8,903.56 average) -- a jump of over PLN 1,000/month in one year. Secondary sources dated before 9 Feb 2026 still show the stale 2025 figure. Poland's Blue Card threshold is notably one of the lowest in the EU for 2026 -- roughly EUR 37,200/year, well below Germany's EUR 50,700 -- per a multi-country 2026 salary-threshold comparison (ep-advisory.com), making Poland's Blue Card a comparatively accessible route relative to its Western European peers, a genuine structural finding worth surfacing on any cross-country Blue Card comparison view. A significant 2025 Act on Foreigners amendment (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 619) abolished the labour-market test for Blue Card applicants and simplified employer-switching (notification only, no fresh permit procedure) -- corroborated by both ATL Law's 2026 guide and mos.cudzoziemcy.gov.pl's own Blue Card FAQ ('Nie, wniosek... test rynku pracy... został zniesiony'), so treated as verified; the exact amendment article number in the primary statutory text (isap.sejm.gov.pl) was not independently pulled in this pass and would be the next-level citation if needed. Contract-length minimum corrected during validation from an initially-drafted 1 year down to the tier-1-confirmed 6 months (mos.cudzoziemcy.gov.pl) -- a real catch worth flagging in its own right, since several tier-3 secondary sources conflate the Blue Card's 6-month minimum with the Single Permit's longer typical contract lengths. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the standard 5-year Polish continuous-residence path pending confirmation of whether Blue Card time earns any acceleration under Polish naturalisation practice specifically (unlike Germany, no accelerated 21-month track was found for Poland's Blue Card in this research pass -- flagged as an open question, not asserted as settled).
